correctness.rationale: Complete finite split representations: every n-vertex split graph occurs among all clique sizes k and nondecreasing sequences of n-k bitmasks on k positions. Exhaustive C++17 code enumerates 1,592,513 representations at order ten and all smaller ones, refines exact frequency-vector colours, and tests every unresolved same-colour vertex pair for a full graph automorphism via complete constrained backtracking. Zero failures through nine; 71 at ten. All 71 have intrinsic strict clique/independent degree separation, so canonicalization under all k! clique permutations and independent-column sorting exactly classifies full-graph isomorphism into 4 families with multiplicities 6,10,10,45. Separate incidence-permutation enumeration verifies all smaller orders; independently implemented Python degree-preserving graph-automorphism enumeration verifies all four ten-vertex representatives and their orbit profiles. The argument proves only this finite cutoff, no infinite-family extrapolation.

value.rationale: The first non-refinable order within the natural hereditary split-graph family and exhaustive classification of all four first failures are meaningful structural invariants, not an arbitrary chosen example. The sharp cutoff sharpens the known wider chordal/outerplanar obstruction context, and the two distinct stable-versus-orbit size patterns reveal specific limitations of local neighbour-count refinement. The computation establishes a mathematically motivated complete finite obstruction layer while explicitly not promising a larger general theorem.
